title: What an embedding is: meaning turned into a vector

videos.script: A customer asks a help centre how to get her money back. The answer is right there, in an article about refunds. {{question}} A search for her words finds the wrong article, about gifts, and misses the right one. She said money back. The article says refund. {{grep}} This lesson is about the idea that fixes that. An embedding turns a piece of text into a list of numbers. {{numbers}} The numbers are chosen so that texts with similar meanings get similar lists. Comparing meanings becomes arithmetic. {{compare}} You will compute one with a small open model, on your own machine, and see what it is made of. Three hundred and eighty-four numbers, every time. {{vector}} Then you will score six articles against the customer's question and watch the refund articles rise to the top. {{scores}} You will flatten the space into a picture and see the categories appear on their own. {{picture}} And you will find the edges. A sentence and its negation look almost the same. Portuguese looks like noise to an English model. {{limits}} Those edges decide where embeddings belong, and the rest of the course is built on them. {{end}}
